scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: A misleading alert comparison
scenes.caption: Kabir sees a summary claiming that alerts increased from twenty to thirty, so the new rule caused a deterioration. The two windows differ in duration and number of observed readings. Some readings are missing in the second window.
scenes.dialogue: A raw count needs a denominator and a time window.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: Read the supplied windows
scenes.caption: Window A has twenty flagged records among one hundred observed readings in one hour, with no missing readings. Window B has thirty flags among three hundred observed readings in three hours, plus fifteen missing readings.
scenes.dialogue: Missing is not another word for normal.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Compare like with like
scenes.caption: The observed-reading flag rates are twenty percent and ten percent. The alert counts per hour also differ from raw totals. Keep the time windows, observed denominators and missingness on the comparison rather than treating missing readings as known negatives.
scenes.dialogue: A corrected table can change the interpretation.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Choose the causal claim
scenes.caption: Do these two windows prove that the new rule caused any change, or do different workloads, windows and missingness leave alternative explanations? Choose the statement supported by this observational pack.
scenes.dialogue: Association alone does not establish the cause.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: A cautious interpretation
scenes.caption: Kabir replaces the raw-count headline with a labelled comparison. The observed flag rate is lower in B in this pack, but missing readings and different conditions limit the conclusion. No controlled comparison establishes why it changed.
scenes.dialogue: A useful summary records its uncertainty.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Enter the summary lab
scenes.caption: Calculate the observed rates, repair the misleading table and state the limits of a causal claim. Keep unknown readings separate and name a plausible alternative explanation to investigate.
scenes.dialogue: A denominator is part of the evidence.
